carrier.proof_tex:
Fix rational \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) and rational \(b\), and put \(N=N_m\).  For \(q\in K_{\epsilon}\), define
\[
 d(q)=p(q)\{1-p(q)\},
 \qquad a(q)=q_{11}\{1-p(q)\}-q_{01}p(q).
\tag{1}
\]
The overlap restriction gives \(d(q)\geq\epsilon(1-\epsilon)>0\) and \(f(q)=a(q)/d(q)\).

Let \(\Phi_N(b,t)\) assert the existence of locations \(q^1,\ldots,q^N\in K_{\epsilon}\) and weights \(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_N\geq0\) such that
\[
 \sum_{k=1}^N\omega_k=1,
 \qquad
 b_c=\sum_{k=1}^N\omega_kB_c^{(m)}(q^k)
 \quad(c\in\mathcal I_m),
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 t\prod_{k=1}^Nd(q^k)
 =\sum_{k=1}^N\omega_ka(q^k)
   \prod_{\substack{1\leq r\leq N\\r\neq k}}d(q^r).
\tag{3}
\]
Every factor cleared in (3) is strictly positive, so (3) is equivalent to \(t=\sum_k\omega_kf(q^k)\).  The simplex, overlap, mass, moment, and objective restrictions are therefore a finite first-order polynomial formula with rational coefficients.

Every \(t\) satisfying \(\Phi_N(b,t)\) is generated by a measure in \(\mathcal F_{m,\epsilon}(b)\).  Conversely, the all-feasible endpoint compression in the sharp primal--dual theorem supplies \(N\)-atom measures attaining both endpoints whenever \(b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\).  Therefore
\[
 \exists t\,\Phi_N(b,t)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon},
\tag{4}
\]
and, when feasible,
\[
 \min\{t:\Phi_N(b,t)\}=L_m(b),
 \qquad
 \max\{t:\Phi_N(b,t)\}=U_m(b).
\tag{5}
\]
This uses only the \(N\)-atom endpoint result and does not assert the same cap for every interior value.  The parameter space \(\Delta_{N-1}\times K_{\epsilon}^N\) is compact and the fixed-\(b\) constraints are closed, so the extrema and their witnesses are attained.

The formulas
\[
 \begin{split}
 G_L(b,t)&\Longleftrightarrow
 \Phi_N(b,t)\wedge\forall s\{\Phi_N(b,s)\Rightarrow t\leq s\},\\
 G_U(b,t)&\Longleftrightarrow
 \Phi_N(b,t)\wedge\forall s\{\Phi_N(b,s)\Rightarrow s\leq t\}
 \end{split}
\tag{6}
\]
define exactly the lower and upper endpoints.  The cited complete CAD quantifier-elimination result applies to (1)--(6): it terminates, decides (4), and, if feasible, returns algebraic endpoint values and algebraic sample points for endpoint locations and weights.  Each endpoint has a rational defining polynomial and rational isolating interval.  Factoring the defining polynomial over \(\mathbb Q\), selecting the unique irreducible factor with a root in the isolating interval, and refining that interval if necessary terminates and returns its minimal polynomial and a rational isolating interval.

Suppose \(b\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\).  The sharp primal--dual theorem supplies attained \(\lambda^-\) and \(\lambda^+\).  Lower global feasibility is
\[
 q\in K_{\epsilon}\Longrightarrow
 d(q)\sum_c\lambda_cB_c^{(m)}(q)\leq a(q),
\tag{7}
\]
and upper feasibility reverses the inequality.  Positivity of \(d(q)\) makes (7) equivalent to the rational Bernstein minorant inequality, and every term is polynomial.  Lower complementary contact for the variables in (2)--(3) is
\[
 \omega_k\left\{a(q^k)-d(q^k)\sum_c\lambda_cB_c^{(m)}(q^k)\right\}=0
 \quad(1\leq k\leq N),
\tag{8}
\]
together with \(\lambda^{\top}b=t\); the upper system uses the reversed slack.  Thus the relative-interior primal--dual branch is a first-order real-algebraic formula.  Strong duality and contact from the sharp primal--dual theorem prove feasibility exactly at \(L_m(b)\) and \(U_m(b)\), so complete CAD returns matching globally feasible dual certificates and at most \(N\) endpoint atoms.

For arbitrary rational \(b\), the boundary branch uses only (2)--(6); dual nonattainment cannot affect primal feasibility or either endpoint.  After the primal outputs, matching lower-certificate existence is the separate first-order sentence
\[
 \exists\lambda\left[
 \lambda^{\top}b=L_m(b),\quad
 \forall q\{q\in K_{\epsilon}\Rightarrow d(q)\lambda^{\top}g_m(q)\leq a(q)\}
 \right],
\tag{9}
\]
and the upper sentence reverses the inequality and substitutes \(U_m(b)\).  Complete CAD decides both.  If either is false, the procedure reports the boundary/nonattainment flag while retaining the certified primal endpoint and witness.  Finally, the SCM moment-reduction lemma converts each atomic measure into a compatible member of \(\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}\) with the same count law and causal endpoint.  This proves exact termination and the stated output semantics; it makes no practical-runtime claim.

Let \(H_{m,\epsilon}:=\operatorname{conv}\{(g_m(q),f(q)):q\in K_{\epsilon}\}\). The set \(H_{m,\epsilon}\) is compact and equals
\[
 \left\{\left(\int g_m\,d\nu,\int f\,d\nu\right):
 \nu\in\mathcal P(K_{\epsilon})\right\}.
\]
Every pair in \(H_{m,\epsilon}\) has a representing probability measure supported on at most \(N_m+1\) points of \(K_{\epsilon}\), and therefore has a compatible hierarchical SCM in \(\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}\) with at most \(N_m+1\) latent cluster laws. If \(b\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\), then \(D_m(b)=(L_m(b),U_m(b))\) with both dual extrema attained. If an optimal dual polynomial has contact image of affine dimension \(r\), its associated endpoint admits at most \(r+1\) atoms.

carrier.proof_tex:
Fix \(m\geq1\) and rational \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), and write \(N=N_m\) and \(K=K_{\epsilon}\).  For \(q\in K\), put
\[
 d(q)=p(q)\{1-p(q)\},
 \qquad a(q)=q_{11}\{1-p(q)\}-q_{01}p(q).
\tag{1}
\]
Then \(d(q)\geq\epsilon(1-\epsilon)>0\) and \(f(q)=a(q)/d(q)\).

For \(1\leq k\leq N\), let \(\Phi_k(b,t)\) assert that there exist \(q^1,\ldots,q^k\in K\) and \(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_k\geq0\) satisfying
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^k\omega_j=1,
 \qquad
 b_c=\sum_{j=1}^k\omega_jB_c^{(m)}(q^j)
 \quad(c\in\mathcal I_m),
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 t\prod_{j=1}^kd(q^j)
 =\sum_{j=1}^k\omega_ja(q^j)
 \prod_{\substack{1\leq r\leq k\\r\neq j}}d(q^r).
\tag{3}
\]
Strict positivity in (1) makes (3) equivalent to \(t=\sum_j\omega_jf(q^j)\).  Thus \(\Phi_k\) is a first-order formula in rational polynomial equalities and weak inequalities.  Zero weights and repeated locations show that it expresses an atomic witness with support size at most \(k\).

Let \(\Phi=\Phi_N\).  Every \(\Phi(b,t)\) witness lies in the moment fiber.  Conversely, the all-feasible endpoint result of the sharp primal--dual theorem gives, for every feasible \(b\), measures with at most \(N\) atoms attaining both endpoints.  Hence
\[
 \Psi(b):\Longleftrightarrow\exists t\,\Phi(b,t)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon},
\tag{4}
\]
and
\[
 \min\{t:\Phi(b,t)\}=L_m(b),
 \qquad
 \max\{t:\Phi(b,t)\}=U_m(b).
\tag{5}
\]
The parameter space \(\Delta_{N-1}\times K^N\) is compact and the barycenter map is continuous, so both extrema in (5) are attained.  Complete CAD quantifier elimination applied to (4) gives a quantifier-free semialgebraic definition of the moment body.

We define the relative rather than ambient boundary.  A first-order definition of \(A=\operatorname{aff}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\subseteq\mathbb R^N\) is
\[
 \operatorname{Aff}(x):\Longleftrightarrow
 \exists z^0,\ldots,z^N\ \exists\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_N
 \left[
 \bigwedge_{j=0}^N\Psi(z^j),\quad
 \sum_{j=0}^N\alpha_j=1,\quad
 x=\sum_{j=0}^N\alpha_jz^j
 \right].
\tag{6}
\]
The right side lies in the affine hull.  Conversely, affine dependence shortens any affine representation in \(\mathbb R^N\) to at most \(N+1\) points while preserving the coefficient sum, so (6) is exact.  Define
\[
 \begin{split}
 \operatorname{RI}(b):\Longleftrightarrow{}&\Psi(b)\wedge
 \exists\rho>0\ \forall x\left[
 \operatorname{Aff}(x)\wedge\sum_c(x_c-b_c)^2<\rho^2
 \Rightarrow\Psi(x)\right],\\
 \operatorname{RB}(b):\Longleftrightarrow{}&\Psi(b)\wedge\neg\operatorname{RI}(b).
 \end{split}
\tag{7}
\]
Formula \(\operatorname{RI}\) is precisely relative interior in \(A\).  The moment body is compact by (4), hence closed in \(A\); therefore \(\operatorname{RB}\) defines exactly \(\operatorname{relbd}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\).  Complete quantifier elimination makes these predicates semialgebraic.

Define endpoint graphs by
\[
 \begin{split}
 G_L(b,t)&\Longleftrightarrow
 \Phi(b,t)\wedge\forall s\{\Phi(b,s)\Rightarrow t\leq s\},\\
 G_U(b,t)&\Longleftrightarrow
 \Phi(b,t)\wedge\forall s\{\Phi(b,s)\Rightarrow s\leq t\}.
 \end{split}
\tag{8}
\]
By compactness and (5), each graph has exactly one value over every feasible \(b\), namely \(L_m(b)\) or \(U_m(b)\).  Consequently
\[
 P_0(b):\Longleftrightarrow\exists t\{G_L(b,t)\wedge G_U(b,t)\}
\tag{9}
\]
is exactly the predicate \(L_m(b)=U_m(b)\).  Since the full sharp fiber is the nonempty interval \([L_m(b),U_m(b)]\), its affine dimension is zero when (9) holds and one otherwise.

For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), \(1\leq k\leq N\), define
\[
 E_{e,k}(b):\Longleftrightarrow
 \exists t\{G_e(b,t)\wedge\Phi_k(b,t)\},
 \qquad E_{e,0}(b):\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{false}.
\tag{10}
\]
These predicates are semialgebraic after quantifier elimination.  Endpoint compression gives \(E_{e,N}(b)\) for every feasible \(b\).  Hence the minimum endpoint support size equals \(k\) exactly when
\[
 S_{e,k}(b):\Longleftrightarrow E_{e,k}(b)\wedge\neg E_{e,k-1}(b),
 \qquad 1\leq k\leq N.
\tag{11}
\]
The negated predicate certifies that no smaller support attains the endpoint.

Complete \(\mathcal A_{m,\epsilon}\) by adjoining (7), (9), and (11) to its face stratification, eliminating all quantified variables, and taking a common truth-invariant CAD in \(b\)-space.  Retain exactly the cells satisfying \(\operatorname{RB}\).  The retained family is finite and semialgebraic.  On each cell, (9), exactly one \(S_{L,k}\), and exactly one \(S_{U,l}\) have constant truth values.  Thus point identification, fiber dimension, and the ordered minimum-support pair are constant, with both support labels in \(\{1,\ldots,N_m\}\).

All coefficients are rational.  The cited complete Collins CAD/QE result therefore proves termination and returns a defining sign formula and an algebraic CAD sample point \(b_C\) for each nonempty retained cell \(C\).  Specialize (8), (10), and the true labels \(S_{L,k}(b_C)\), \(S_{U,l}(b_C)\) at that sample point.  Algebraic coordinates can be encoded by rational minimal-polynomial and isolating-interval constraints, so a further complete rational-coefficient QE/CAD call terminates and returns algebraic endpoint values, atom locations, and weights for \(b_C\). carrier.proof_tex:
Fix \(b'\in\Delta_{N_m-1}\), and let \(W\sim\operatorname{Multinomial}(n,b')\) on the finite set \(\mathcal H_n\).  Write
\[
 v_1>v_2>\cdots>v_J
\]
for the distinct extended-real values of \(T_n(w;b')\), and set
\[
 E_j=\{w:T_n(w;b')\geq v_j\},
 \qquad \pi_j=\Pr_{b'}(W\in E_j).
\tag{1}
\]
The tie-inclusive definition gives \(P_n(b';w)=\pi_j\) whenever \(T_n(w;b')=v_j\).  Since \(E_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq E_J\), one has \(\pi_1\leq\cdots\leq\pi_J\).  If no \(j\) has \(\pi_j\leq\alpha\), rejection is impossible.  Otherwise, for the largest such \(j_*\), the rejection event is exactly \(E_{j_*}\), including the entire tie at \(v_{j_*}\).  Hence
\[
 \Pr_{b'}\{P_n(b';W)\leq\alpha\}
 =\pi_{j_*}\leq\alpha.
\tag{2}
\]
If a deviance is infinite because a positive count falls in a zero-probability cell, that sample point has probability zero under \(b'\), so (2) also covers infinite values.

For each \(S\subseteq\mathcal I_m\), consider the zero-pattern cell
\[
 D_S=\{b'\in\Delta_{N_m-1}:b'_c>0\Longleftrightarrow c\in S\}.
\tag{3}
\]
There are finitely many such semialgebraic cells.  For \(x\in\mathcal H_n\), put
\[
 a_x=\prod_{c:x_c>0}\left(\frac{x_c}{n}\right)^{x_c}\in\mathbb Q_{>0}.
\tag{4}
\]
On \(D_S\), \(T_n(x;b')\) is finite exactly when \(\{c:x_c>0\}\subseteq S\).  If both \(T_n(w;b')\) and \(T_n(z;b')\) are finite, strict monotonicity of exponentiation and positivity of \(b'_c\) on \(S\) give
\[
 T_n(w;b')\geq T_n(z;b')
 \Longleftrightarrow
 a_w\prod_{c\in S}(b'_c)^{z_c}
 \geq a_z\prod_{c\in S}(b'_c)^{w_c}.
\tag{5}
\]
After clearing a positive integer denominator, the right side is a rational polynomial inequality.  If a deviance is infinite, the extended-real comparison has a fixed truth value on \(D_S\).  Thus every fixed deviance comparison is semialgebraic on each zero-pattern cell.

Partition each \(D_S\) further according to the finitely many comparisons with \(z=z^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  On a resulting cell the tail set \(J(b')\) is constant, and
\[
 P_n(b';z^{\mathrm{obs}})
 =\sum_{w\in J(b')}\frac{n!}{\prod_cw_c!}\prod_c(b'_c)^{w_c}
\tag{6}
\]
is a polynomial.  Hence \(P_n(b';z^{\mathrm{obs}})>\alpha\) is a strict polynomial inequality there.  The finite union over all cells proves that \(\mathcal R_{n,\alpha}(z^{\mathrm{obs}})\) is semialgebraic.

The attainable-pair result and \((N_m+1)\)-atom representation in the sharp primal--dual theorem show that \(t\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(z^{\mathrm{obs}})\) is equivalent to the existence of \(b'\), \(q^1,\ldots,q^{N_m+1}\in K_{\epsilon}\), and \(\omega_k\geq0\) such that
\[
 \begin{split}
 &\sum_{k=1}^{N_m+1}\omega_k=1,
 \qquad b'_c=\sum_{k=1}^{N_m+1}\omega_kB_c^{(m)}(q^k)
 \quad(c\in\mathcal I_m),\\
 &t=\sum_{k=1}^{N_m+1}\omega_kf(q^k),
 \qquad b'\in\mathcal R_{n,\alpha}(z^{\mathrm{obs}}).
 \end{split}
\tag{7}
\]
Zero masses pad shorter representations.  Thus (7) is exactly the whole causal union, not a relaxation over unrelated moments.

If \(\epsilon\), \(\alpha\), and \(z^{\mathrm{obs}}\) are rational, membership in \(K_{\epsilon}\) is expressed by rational polynomial simplex and overlap inequalities.  Every Bernstein equation is polynomial.  Since each \(p(q^k)\) and \(1-p(q^k)\) is at least \(\epsilon>0\), multiplication of the objective equation by their product preserves equivalence and yields a rational polynomial equality.  Together with (3)--(6), formula (7) is therefore first order over \(\mathbb Q\).  The cited complete CAD result eliminates all variables except \(t\), terminates, and returns a semialgebraic decomposition of the resulting subset of the real line.

For every \(q\in K_{\epsilon}\), positivity and the simplex inequalities imply
\[
 0\leq\frac{q_{11}}{p(q)}\leq1,
 \qquad 0\leq\frac{q_{01}}{1-p(q)}\leq1.
\]
Hence \(-1\leq f(q)\leq1\), so (7) implies \(t\in[-1,1]\).  A semialgebraic subset of the line is a finite disjoint union of points and intervals.  Complete CAD represents finite boundaries by rational defining polynomials and rational isolating intervals; evaluation of the quantifier-free sign formula at a boundary decides inclusion.  Thus \(\operatorname{CAD}^{\mathrm{conf}}_{m,n}\) returns the full decomposition with open-or-closed flags.  Alternatively, it may select the leftmost and rightmost boundaries and test membership there, yielding the certified endpoint hull with attainability flags.  If the set is empty, it returns the empty certificate.  This proves the stated finite exact semantics, without a runtime bound.

Its inversion \(\mathcal R_{n,\alpha}(z^{\mathrm{obs}})\) is semialgebraic: on each zero-pattern cell, every deviance comparison is equivalent after exponentiation and positive-denominator clearing to a monomial polynomial inequality, and \(P_n\) is a finite polynomial sum. By the SCM moment-reduction lemma, under every \((\mu,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}\), the cluster counts are iid with categorical law \(b\), so \(Z\sim\operatorname{Multinomial}(n,b)\), and \(b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\).  The size bound in the finite-complexity inference theorem, applied at the true \(b\), gives
\[
 \Pr_{\mathcal M}\{b\notin\mathcal R_{n,\alpha}(Z)\}
 =\Pr_{\mathcal M}\{P_n(b;Z)\leq\alpha\}\leq\alpha.
\]
On the complementary event, \(b\) is one of the candidates in \(\mathcal R_{n,\alpha}(Z)\cap\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\).  The defining union for \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(Z)\) therefore contains its entire sharp fiber:
\[
 [L_m(b),U_m(b)]\subseteq\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(Z).
\]
Taking probabilities proves the \(1-\alpha\) guarantee.  The argument uses no law-specific constant, hence is uniform over \(\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}\).  It invokes neither relative interior nor positive width and thus includes boundary laws with singleton fibers.

carrier.proof_tex:
Write \(K=K_{\epsilon}\), \(V=V_m\), and \(d=d_m(\epsilon)\).  Compactness of \(K\) and continuity of \(f\) make the uniform norm finite.  The identity \(\sum_{c\in\mathcal I_m}B_c^{(m)}=1\) shows that \(1\in V\).

We first prove the universal upper bound by moment cancellation.  Fix \(b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\) and \(\nu_1,\nu_0\in\mathcal F_{m,\epsilon}(b)\).  For \(\zeta=\nu_1-\nu_0\), the defining constraints of the fiber imply
\[
 \int B_c^{(m)}\,d\zeta=0\quad(c\in\mathcal I_m),
\]
and hence \(\int v\,d\zeta=0\) for every \(v\in V\).  Since \(\nu_1\) and \(\nu_0\) are probabilities, \(\|\zeta\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\leq2\).  Thus, for every \(v\in V\),
\[
 \left|\int f\,d\nu_1-\int f\,d\nu_0\right|
 =\left|\int(f-v)\,d\zeta\right|
 \leq\|f-v\|_{\infty,K}\|\zeta\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq2\|f-v\|_{\infty,K}.
\]
Taking the infimum over \(v\), and then the supremum over ordered pairs in the same nonempty fiber, gives
\[
 U_m(b)-L_m(b)\leq2d. \tag{1}
\]
Here the equality of the width with the pairwise supremum follows directly from \(\sup a-\inf a=\sup_{a_1,a_0}(a_1-a_0)\); endpoint attainment is not needed for this step.

We next prove that the factor two in (1) is exact.  The space \(V\) is finite dimensional and therefore closed in \(C(K)\).  The finite-plate nonpolynomial lemma gives \(f\notin V\).  The Hahn--Banach quotient-norm theorem therefore yields a bounded real linear functional \(\Lambda\) on \(C(K)\) such that
\[
 \|\Lambda\|=1,\qquad \Lambda(v)=0\ (v\in V),\qquad \Lambda(f)=d,
\]
where the sign is chosen so that the last display is nonnegative.  The Riesz--Markov representation and Jordan decomposition give a finite signed regular Borel measure \(\sigma=\sigma^+-\sigma^-\) satisfying
\[
 \Lambda(u)=\int_Ku\,d\sigma,qquad
 \sigma^+(K)+\sigma^-(K)=|\sigma|(K)=1. \tag{2}
\]
The normalization is forced, rather than assumed.  Since \(1\in V\),
\[
 0=\Lambda(1)=\sigma(K)=\sigma^+(K)-\sigma^-(K).
\]
Combining this equality with (2) gives
\[
 \sigma^+(K)=\sigma^-(K)=\frac12.
\]
Therefore \(\nu_+=2\sigma^+\) and \(\nu_-=2\sigma^-\) are probability measures.  For every \(c\in\mathcal I_m\), annihilation of \(V\) gives
\[
 \int B_c^{(m)}\,d\nu_+-\int B_c^{(m)}\,d\nu_-
 =2\int B_c^{(m)}\,d\sigma=0.
\]
They consequently share a feasible moment vector \(b_*\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\), while
\[
 \int f\,d\nu_+-\int f\,d\nu_-
 =2\int f\,d\sigma=2\Lambda(f)=2d. \tag{3}
\]
Equation (1) and the two compatible measures in (3) prove
\[
 \max_{b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}}\{U_m(b)-L_m(b)\}=2d; \tag{4}
\]
in particular, the maximum in (4) is attained at \(b_*\).

It remains to show that restricting to relative-interior moment vectors leaves the same supremum.  Choose \(b_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\) and, by the definition of the moment body, choose one representing probability \(\eta\in\mathcal F_{m,\epsilon}(b_0)\).  For \(0\leq t<1\), set
\[
 \nu_{t,+}=(1-t)\eta+t\nu_+,qquad
 \nu_{t,-}=(1-t)\eta+t\nu_-,qquad
 b_t=(1-t)b_0+tb_*.
\]
Linearity of the Bernstein moments puts both measures in \(\mathcal F_{m,\epsilon}(b_t)\).  Also \(b_t\) is in the relative interior: if a relative ball of radius \(r>0\) about \(b_0\) lies in the moment body, then the relative ball of radius \((1-t)r\) about \(b_t\) lies there by convexity.  From (3),
\[
 U_m(b_t)-L_m(b_t)
 \geq\int f\,d\nu_{t,+}-\int f\,d\nu_{t,-}
 =2td.
\]
Letting \(t\uparrow1\), then using (1), proves
\[
 \sup_{b\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})}
 \{U_m(b)-L_m(b)\}=2d. \tag{5}
\]

We now bound \(d\) constructively.  Put
\[
 x=2p(q)-1,qquad \rho=1-2\epsilon.
\]
The overlap restriction \(\epsilon\leq p(q)\leq1-\epsilon\) gives \(|x|\leq\rho<1\), while \(1+x=2p(q)>0\) and \(1-x=2\{1-p(q)\}>0\).  Define
\[
 v_m(q)=2q_{11}\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}(-x)^k
          -2q_{01}\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}x^k
          -\mathbf 1_{\{m\ {\rm odd}\}}x^m. \tag{6}
\]
The function in (6) is the restriction to the simplex of a polynomial of total degree at most \(m\): \(x\) has degree one, and the first two terms multiply powers of degree at most \(m-1\) by one cell coordinate.  By the finite-plate polynomial-span lemma, \(v_m\in V_m\).

The finite geometric identities
\[
 \frac1{1+x}=\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}(-x)^k+\frac{(-x)^m}{1+x},
 \qquad
 \frac1{1-x}=\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}x^k+\frac{x^m}{1-x}
\]
and the equality \(f=2q_{11}/(1+x)-2q_{01}/(1-x)\) give two cases.  If \(m\) is even, then
\[
 f(q)-v_m(q)
 =2x^m\left\{\frac{q_{11}}{1+x}-\frac{q_{01}}{1-x}\right\}. \tag{7}
\]
If \(m\) is odd, the correction \(-x^m\) in (6) gives
\[
 f(q)-v_m(q)
 =x^m\left[1-2\left\{\frac{q_{11}}{1+x}+\frac{q_{01}}{1-x}\right\}\right]. \tag{8}
\]
Because \(q_{11}\leq p(q)=(1+x)/2\) and \(q_{01}\leq1-p(q)=(1-x)/2\),
\[
 0\leq\frac{q_{11}}{1+x}\leq\frac12,
 \qquad
 0\leq\frac{q_{01}}{1-x}\leq\frac12. \tag{9}
\]
The bracket multiplying \(x^m\) has absolute value at most one in both (7) and (8), by (9).  Hence
\[
 \|f-v_m\|_{\infty,K_{\epsilon}}\leq\rho^m=(1-2\epsilon)^m,
\]
which proves \(d_m(\epsilon)\leq(1-2\epsilon)^m\).

Finally, finite dimensionality makes \(V_m\) closed in \(C(K_{\epsilon})\).  The finite-plate nonpolynomial lemma gives \(f\notin V_m\), so its distance from this closed subspace is strictly positive: \(d_m(\epsilon)>0\).  Combining this fact with (4), (5), and the constructive upper bound proves all modulus assertions.  For \(0<\delta\leq2\), the displayed plate-size condition and \(-\log(1-2\epsilon)>0\) imply \(2(1-2\epsilon)^m\leq\delta\); applying (1) proves the final simultaneous guarantee.  This is a deterministic uniform identification-width rate in \(m\), not a sampling rate in \(n\).

semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Each \(B_c^{(m)}\) is a scalar multiple of a monomial of total degree \(m\), so \(V_m\) consists of restrictions of polynomials of total degree at most \(m\).  Conversely, on the simplex \(\sum_{a,y}q_{ay}=1\).  If \(q^{\gamma}\) is a monomial of degree \(d\leq m\), then
\[
 q^{\gamma}=q^{\gamma}\left(\sum_{a,y}q_{ay}\right)^{m-d},
\]
and the multinomial expansion on the right is a linear combination of total-degree-\(m\) monomials, hence of the Bernstein polynomials \(B_c^{(m)}\).  Thus \(V_m\) is exactly the asserted restriction space.

Suppose for contradiction that a polynomial \(P\) agrees with \(f\) on \(K_{\epsilon}\).  Put \(a=\epsilon/2>0\), and for \(r\in(\epsilon,1-\epsilon)\) consider
\[
 q(r)=(q_{00},q_{01},q_{10},q_{11})=(1-r,0,r-a,a).
\]
All four coordinates are nonnegative and \(p(q(r))=r\), so this path lies in \(K_{\epsilon}\).  The function \(R(r)=P(q(r))\) is a polynomial in \(r\), while
\[
 f(q(r))=\frac{a}{r}.
\]
Consequently the polynomial \(rR(r)-a\) vanishes on the nonempty open interval \((\epsilon,1-\epsilon)\) and therefore is identically zero.  Evaluating that polynomial identity at \(r=0\) gives \(-a=0\), a contradiction.  Hence \(f\) is not the restriction of any polynomial, and in particular \(f\notin V_m\) for every finite \(m\).

payload.tldr: Fixed-size cluster counts reveal only degree-\(m\) Bernstein moments of latent four-cell exposure--outcome laws, so the cluster-equally-weighted ATE is generally an interval rather than a point. Each hierarchical SCM carries \(\mu\in\mathcal P(K_{\epsilon})\), draws \(Q_i\sim\mu\), and calibrates the observed four-cell law to \(Q_i\). The sharp interval has attained measure and Bernstein-polynomial programs at every relative-interior count law, with compatible endpoint SCMs using at most \({m+3\choose3}\) latent laws. Its exact worst-case width is \(2d_m(\epsilon)\), where \(d_m(\epsilon)\) is the uniform distance from the nonlinear ATE integrand to the degree-\(m\) Bernstein span; \(0<d_m(\epsilon)\leq(1-2\epsilon)^m\) yields an explicit exponential plate-size elbow. The paper also proves a finite truth-invariant semialgebraic stratification of the entire relative boundary, with a certified algebraic sample point and minimum-support endpoint witnesses for every nonempty cell; it does not claim that a concrete atlas was executed, that CAD is practically fast, or that a uniform symbolic witness map exists on positive-dimensional cells. For an arbitrary supplied algebraic count law, witnesses are recovered by specialization and a fresh terminating CAD run. A generic contact-hull theorem characterizes equality with valid count-measurable envelopes, and exact multinomial likelihood inversion gives uniform whole-identified-set coverage and a semialgebraic confidence set.

project_justification.gap: The S\~ao Paulo DOT analysis shows that city random-effect choices move the posterior ATE, while fixed-plate mixture theory establishes finite-moment information loss without characterizing this causal functional. Existing limited-pooling ATE bounds use particular valid polynomials, and generalized-moment theory does not supply the hierarchical SCM semantics, the iff identification frontier, the exact uniform identification-width modulus, or a truth-invariant stratification of the entire relative boundary with minimum-support endpoint labels.
project_justification.niche: The observable cluster-count law is finite dimensional, but the latent city law is unrestricted and the causal target is a nonlinear reciprocal functional under overlap. This creates a tractable convex moment geometry in which fixed finite plates never identify the ATE uniformly, increasing plate size shrinks the worst-case sharp interval at an explicit exponential rate, and boundary precision can be classified exactly by finite real algebraic tests.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives the sharp primal--dual interval, proves an iff Bernstein-span identification frontier and strict width throughout the relative interior, identifies the exact maximal width as twice a best uniform polynomial-approximation error, and proves \(2d_m(\epsilon)\leq2(1-2\epsilon)^m\) with an explicit plate-size elbow. It constructs finite-latent endpoint SCMs, proves a finite truth-invariant semialgebraic stratification of the entire relative boundary with minimum-support labels and sample-point witnesses, gives an exact contact-hull criterion and strict improvement regions for valid degree-\(m\) envelopes with the scalar-reference limited-pooling transplant as a corollary, and turns exact multinomial inversion into a one-dimensional semialgebraic confidence set with uniform whole-set coverage and terminating CAD recovery. The CAD claims concern exact termination and on-demand specialization, not an executed atlas, practical runtime, or a uniform symbolic witness map over positive-dimensional cells.

payload.related_work: Nobre, Schmidt, Moodie, and Stephens (2023, Sections 5--6 and Figure 3) motivate the problem by documenting ATE sensitivity to city random effects in the S\~ao Paulo DOT study. Wood (1999, Introduction and Sections 2--4, especially Example 2 on pp. 1717--1718) develops fixed-binomial convex geometry and exhibits a polygonal nonidentifiable slice but does not study a four-cell causal functional, an iff Bernstein-span frontier, a uniform identification-width modulus, or a truth-invariant classification of the whole relative boundary. Wood (1992, p. 1167) connects binomial-mixture membership to infinite extendibility of a finite exchangeable Bernoulli law; this is background for the repeated-observation interpretation, not a causal-functional comparator. Rosenbaum and Rubin (1983) provide the standard conditional-ignorability framework and Rubin (1974) the potential-outcome framework underlying consistency; here ignorability is imposed conditional on latent \(Q_i\), and these assumptions map calibrated observed cells to the causal integrand. Lee and Weidner (2026) study an observed discrete-covariate conditional-factorization class with an \(x\)-dependent reference propensity. That class and experiment are not the present latent-\(Q\) mixing experiment: only their pointwise population envelope transfers after conditioning on \(Q=q\) and integrating over \(q\), whereas their sample and asymptotic procedure does not transfer. Accordingly, the paper compares only the explicitly defined scalar-reference, count-law-only population transplant, whose validity is proved directly, and not their full covariate-dependent estimator or inference theory. Bertsimas and Popescu (2005, Theorem 2.2) inform the generalized-moment duality argument. Halaseh, Magron, and Skomra (2026, Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 5.9) inform dual attainment and full-support representation for polynomial moment problems, but their objectives are polynomial, whereas \(f\) is rational on \(K_{\epsilon}\); the present result is therefore not a literal specialization. Bayer and Teichmann (2006, Theorem 1) inform atomic compression, while Winkler (1988, Theorem 2.1(b)) clarifies that support size alone does not characterize extremality. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjölander, and Gabriel (2023, Sections 2--4) derive tight symbolic bounds by linear programming and vertex enumeration for categorical causal DAGs after finite response-function reduction, with linear observed-probability constraints and a linear causal query. They do not treat an unrestricted Borel mixing law over a continuous four-cell simplex, Bernstein moment fibers with the rational ATE functional, the finite-atom endpoint reduction, or CAD stratification and recovery. Duarte et al. (2023, Proposition 1 and Algorithm 1) compute numerical polynomial causal bounds for finite discrete SCMs; the present continuous-latent problem first requires endpoint compression and then exact quantifier elimination. England, Bradford, and Davenport (2020, Theorem 1 and Algorithm 1) supply the CAD machinery. Here CAD proves a finite truth-invariant semialgebraic stratification of the entire relative boundary and supports fresh witness recovery after specializing any supplied algebraic \(b\); no executed atlas, practical-runtime claim, or uniform symbolic witness map over a positive-dimensional cell is attributed to that machinery. Bugni (2010, Theorems 1--3) motivates whole-set coverage, while Basu, Brill, and Yekutieli (2026, Section 4) motivate exact finite-sample inversion; neither source proves that the inverted hierarchical ATE set is semialgebraic or CAD-recoverable.

payload.statement: For every fixed \(m\geq1\) and rational \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the relative boundary \(\operatorname{relbd}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\), taken in \(\operatorname{aff}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\), admits a finite truth-invariant semialgebraic stratification on each cell of which the indicator of \(L_m(b)=U_m(b)\), the affine dimension \(0\) or \(1\) of \(\Theta_{m,\epsilon}(b)\), and the ordered pair of minimum lower- and upper-endpoint support sizes are constant.  Both minimum sizes lie in \(\{1,\ldots,N_m\}\).  The construction \(\mathcal A_{m,\epsilon}\), completed by the quantified endpoint and support-size tests in the proof, is a terminating CAD procedure that returns defining formulas, the constant support labels, and one algebraic sample point with endpoint witnesses of the certified minimum sizes for every nonempty cell.  It does not return a uniform symbolic endpoint-witness map over a positive-dimensional cell.  For any separately supplied algebraic \(b\) on the relative boundary, specialization followed by a fresh terminating QE/CAD run returns endpoint witnesses having the certified minimum support sizes at that \(b\).
payload.proof_tex:
Fix \(m\geq1\) and rational \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), and write \(N=N_m\) and \(K=K_{\epsilon}\).  For \(q\in K\), put
\[
 d(q)=p(q)\{1-p(q)\},
 \qquad a(q)=q_{11}\{1-p(q)\}-q_{01}p(q).
\tag{1}
\]
Then \(d(q)\geq\epsilon(1-\epsilon)>0\) and \(f(q)=a(q)/d(q)\).

For \(1\leq k\leq N\), let \(\Phi_k(b,t)\) assert that there exist \(q^1,\ldots,q^k\in K\) and \(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_k\geq0\) satisfying
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^k\omega_j=1,
 \qquad
 b_c=\sum_{j=1}^k\omega_jB_c^{(m)}(q^j)
 \quad(c\in\mathcal I_m),
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 t\prod_{j=1}^kd(q^j)
 =\sum_{j=1}^k\omega_ja(q^j)
 \prod_{\substack{1\leq r\leq k\\r\neq j}}d(q^r).
\tag{3}
\]
Strict positivity in (1) makes (3) equivalent to \(t=\sum_j\omega_jf(q^j)\).  Thus \(\Phi_k\) is a first-order formula in rational polynomial equalities and weak inequalities.  Zero weights and repeated locations show that it expresses an atomic witness with support size at most \(k\).

Let \(\Phi=\Phi_N\).  Every \(\Phi(b,t)\) witness lies in the moment fiber.  Conversely, the all-feasible endpoint result of the sharp primal--dual theorem gives, for every feasible \(b\), measures with at most \(N\) atoms attaining both endpoints.  Hence
\[
 \Psi(b):\Longleftrightarrow\exists t\,\Phi(b,t)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon},
\tag{4}
\]
and
\[
 \min\{t:\Phi(b,t)\}=L_m(b),
 \qquad
 \max\{t:\Phi(b,t)\}=U_m(b).
\tag{5}
\]
The parameter space \(\Delta_{N-1}\times K^N\) is compact and the barycenter map is continuous, so both extrema in (5) are attained.  Complete CAD quantifier elimination applied to (4) gives a quantifier-free semialgebraic definition of the moment body.

We define the relative rather than ambient boundary.  A first-order definition of \(A=\operatorname{aff}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\subseteq\mathbb R^N\) is
\[
 \operatorname{Aff}(x):\Longleftrightarrow
 \exists z^0,\ldots,z^N\ \exists\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_N
 \left[
 \bigwedge_{j=0}^N\Psi(z^j),\quad
 \sum_{j=0}^N\alpha_j=1,\quad
 x=\sum_{j=0}^N\alpha_jz^j
 \right].
\tag{6}
\]
The right side lies in the affine hull.  Conversely, affine dependence shortens any affine representation in \(\mathbb R^N\) to at most \(N+1\) points while preserving the coefficient sum, so (6) is exact.  Define
\[
 \begin{split}
 \operatorname{RI}(b):\Longleftrightarrow{}&\Psi(b)\wedge
 \exists\rho>0\ \forall x\left[
 \operatorname{Aff}(x)\wedge\sum_c(x_c-b_c)^2<\rho^2
 \Rightarrow\Psi(x)\right],\\
 \operatorname{RB}(b):\Longleftrightarrow{}&\Psi(b)\wedge\neg\operatorname{RI}(b).
 \end{split}
\tag{7}
\]
Formula \(\operatorname{RI}\) is precisely relative interior in \(A\).  The moment body is compact by (4), hence closed in \(A\); therefore \(\operatorname{RB}\) defines exactly \(\operatorname{relbd}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\).  Complete quantifier elimination makes these predicates semialgebraic.

Define endpoint graphs by
\[
 \begin{split}
 G_L(b,t)&\Longleftrightarrow
 \Phi(b,t)\wedge\forall s\{\Phi(b,s)\Rightarrow t\leq s\},\\
 G_U(b,t)&\Longleftrightarrow
 \Phi(b,t)\wedge\forall s\{\Phi(b,s)\Rightarrow s\leq t\}.
 \end{split}
\tag{8}
\]
By compactness and (5), each graph has exactly one value over every feasible \(b\), namely \(L_m(b)\) or \(U_m(b)\).  Consequently
\[
 P_0(b):\Longleftrightarrow\exists t\{G_L(b,t)\wedge G_U(b,t)\}
\tag{9}
\]
is exactly the predicate \(L_m(b)=U_m(b)\).  Since the full sharp fiber is the nonempty interval \([L_m(b),U_m(b)]\), its affine dimension is zero when (9) holds and one otherwise.

For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), \(1\leq k\leq N\), define
\[
 E_{e,k}(b):\Longleftrightarrow
 \exists t\{G_e(b,t)\wedge\Phi_k(b,t)\},
 \qquad E_{e,0}(b):\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{false}.
\tag{10}
\]
These predicates are semialgebraic after quantifier elimination.  Endpoint compression gives \(E_{e,N}(b)\) for every feasible \(b\).  Hence the minimum endpoint support size equals \(k\) exactly when
\[
 S_{e,k}(b):\Longleftrightarrow E_{e,k}(b)\wedge\neg E_{e,k-1}(b),
 \qquad 1\leq k\leq N.
\tag{11}
\]
The negated predicate certifies that no smaller support attains the endpoint.

Complete \(\mathcal A_{m,\epsilon}\) by adjoining (7), (9), and (11) to its face stratification, eliminating all quantified variables, and taking a common truth-invariant CAD in \(b\)-space.  Retain exactly the cells satisfying \(\operatorname{RB}\).  The retained family is finite and semialgebraic.  On each cell, (9), exactly one \(S_{L,k}\), and exactly one \(S_{U,l}\) have constant truth values.  Thus point identification, fiber dimension, and the ordered minimum-support pair are constant, with both support labels in \(\{1,\ldots,N_m\}\).

All coefficients are rational.  The cited complete Collins CAD/QE result therefore proves termination and returns a defining sign formula and an algebraic CAD sample point \(b_C\) for each nonempty retained cell \(C\).  Specialize (8), (10), and the true labels \(S_{L,k}(b_C)\), \(S_{U,l}(b_C)\) at that sample point.  Algebraic coordinates can be encoded by rational minimal-polynomial and isolating-interval constraints, so a further complete rational-coefficient QE/CAD call terminates and returns algebraic endpoint values, atom locations, and weights for \(b_C\).  If a returned \(k\)-slot representation had zero mass or two equal positive-mass locations, deleting or merging them would give a \((k-1)\)-slot representation, contradicting \(S_{e,k}\).  Thus the cell's sample-point witnesses have the certified minimum sizes.

This construction gives one witness at \(b_C\), not a uniform symbolic choice of atoms and weights over all \(b\in C\).  If an arbitrary algebraic \(b\in C\) is supplied separately, encode each coordinate by a rational polynomial plus isolating interval, specialize the same formulas, and run complete QE/CAD afresh.  The same argument terminates and returns minimum-size endpoint witnesses at that \(b\).  For rational boundary inputs this is the boundary branch of the exact CAD recovery theorem.  No concrete atlas has been executed and no runtime guarantee is inferred from termination.

Finally, the boundary Dirac-regression proposition shows that the point-identified label is nonvacuous when \(m\geq2\):
\[
 \mathcal F_{m,\epsilon}(g_m(q^*))=\{\delta_{q^*}\},
 \qquad L_m(g_m(q^*))=U_m(g_m(q^*))=f(q^*).
\tag{12}
\]
Such a moment vector is extreme, since a nontrivial convex decomposition, followed by mixing representations of its terms, would contradict the singleton fiber.  Moreover, the multinomial first-moment identity gives
\[
 q_{ay}=\frac1m\sum_{c\in\mathcal I_m}c_{ay}B_c^{(m)}(q),
\tag{13}
\]
so \(g_m\) is injective.  The overlap slab contains distinct perturbations of the uniform vector keeping propensity \(1/2\), so the body is not a singleton.  An extreme point of a non-singleton convex set is not in its relative interior.  Hence (12) lies on the relative boundary and receives the zero-dimensional label in (9).  This completes the constructive classification.
